findings.finding: The execution binding and managed revision were permitted only before the loop; a revocation or block between steps did not stop the next spawn.
findings.resolution: Every step after the first rechecks the binding (binding::recheck::current) and the managed revision (session::revision::recheck) under the fence lock, after the fence recheck. Both are the non-writing halves that binding::revalidate and session::revision::permit now call, so the seam subject is the same. A lost binding, a blocked session or a seam error ends the loop without spawning as the retained post-dispatch disposition authority_withdrawn {cause: execution_binding | managed_revision}, with the revalidation record, refusal or error under authority_withdrawn.evidence. Neither binding-revalidation.json nor revision-block.json is written, because inventory projects those as before-dispatch states.

findings.finding: Checks ran against the mutable workspace with no identity check afterwards.
findings.resolution: Each check runs against its own copy of the captured candidate snapshot under repair/check-N-<check>/, written with every write bit removed. After the check the copy is captured again; a changed or uncapturable copy is passed to checks::classify as drifted, which outranks every other defect as checks_rejected {defect: candidate_drift}, and no further check runs. The copy is removed after its check. The worker workspace is never given to a check.

findings.finding: Elapsed time was checked before a spawn only, not after its worker or checks, and a clock lost during a step did not produce clock uncertainty.
findings.resolution: WorkerPort::step and CheckPort::run take a deadline, Loop::remaining_ms, the time left before max_elapsed_ms. The clock is read again before each check, after the worker and after the checks; a reached bound is budget_exhausted {bound: elapsed} and an unreadable clock uncertain {cause: clock}, never a passing disposition.

findings.finding: Policy and lineage bounds were examined only before another spawn, so a final step that overran a budget could still pass.
findings.resolution: Loop::settled compares the charged totals with every policy budget and lineage::Binding::overdrawn after each step's charge (an overrun step is never checked) and again after its checks, before correct_candidate or repaired_candidate. An overrun is budget_exhausted naming the bound.
findings.scenario: tool budget 6; the first step reports 9 and leaves a candidate the unit check would pass; the disposition is budget_exhausted {bound: tool_invocations} and no check runs

findings.finding: A Kiln-owned proposal was handled before an unknown worker outcome.
findings.resolution: Loop::after_step handles cancelled and unknown outcomes before any proposal; unknown plus changed_work is uncertain {cause: worker_outcome}.

findings.finding: Context::load created the state root and attempt directory before the lineage gate.
findings.resolution: Context::load only reads. The state root and attempt directory are created after the lineage gate, the repair ports and the session admission and before fencing::admit takes the lock, so the e3ef038c lock ordering is unchanged. Recovery still creates them before reconciling.
findings.scenario: first-run lineage_exhausted, lineage_blocked and repair_ports_unavailable refusals leave no state root; a lineage_exhausted refusal in an existing state root adds no entry at any depth

findings.finding: Lattice rejected Kiln Alias names such as gpu-seconds.
findings.resolution: Dimension names follow Kiln 339116f6 Alias::new (crates/kiln-core/src/types.rs: BoundedText::new with DEFAULT_MAX_ALIAS_BYTES = 256): non-empty and at most 256 bytes, no narrower grammar. Names Lattice cannot charge are accepted and listed in unaccounted_dimensions.

non_claims: Fixture ports only: no OMP process, check executor, model endpoint or Kiln lineage was exercised.
The shell cannot interrupt a port that ignores its deadline; it detects the overrun when the port returns.
A check that changes its copy and restores the same bytes before returning is not detected as drift.
Pre-write refusals other than lineage_blocked, lineage_exhausted and repair_ports_unavailable were not tested for an unchanged state root.
